svg.title: The design path of Chapter 1 in six steps, each with the artefact it should produce
svg.desc: Ask why, translate into three requirement types, force out unstated constraints, validate against the principles, implement with four techniques, and self-check against three pitfalls. Each step lists the document it leaves behind, from the measured problem statement to the pre-build review checklist.
svg.text: The whole chapter as one sequence of actions
Six steps on the left, the document each one must leave behind on the right
ARTEFACT
Ask "why" — the business objective
until the answer is something you can verify
→ a measured problem statement and a business case,
not a list of technologies
Translate into functional, technical, application
each requirement with a stated level, not a slogan
→ a requirement table in which every line names the
business objective it traces back to
Force out the unstated constraints
budget, compliance, legacy, people, time
→ a constraint register, including the constraints the
customer assumed you already knew
Validate against the six principles
security, availability, scalability, cost, manageability, unstated needs
→ a decision record showing which principle decided
each contested trade-off
Implement with the four techniques
fault isolation, information hiding, modularity, hierarchy
→ a module and layer diagram whose interfaces are
explicit enough to hand over
Self-check against the three pitfalls
assumptions, over-engineering, the best-practice fallacy
→ a review checklist signed before the build starts,
including why the rejected options were rejected
The path is a loop, not a waterfall: a constraint discovered at step 3 sends you back to step 2, and a failed self-check at step 6 sends you back to step 4.
Skip a hop and it does not disappear — it returns later as rework, with the schedule already spent.
